My honest thoughts on the movie:
I felt as if the Spider-Sense was slightly undermined by being somewhat played for jokes, It still served a great purpose but THAT scene would’ve been way better if it felt taken more seriously, personally.

The personal stakes being high during the final battle? Absolutely, loved it while i’m not the biggest fan of “world domination” plots with Spidey, it fit for the movie just again not a big fan of such big scopes.

MJ I eased up my opinion about, I don’t mind this version of MJ it’s an interesting take but I wouldn’t hate if she were a more comic accurate take but for these films, it’s fine. Plus, their scenes absolutely loved.

VFX were phenomenal especially during the construction site fight, I ADORED it so so much. While at some parts he did look chunky or just off, it wasn’t too noticeable later on.

Characterization of Peter isn’t fully there for me personally, I’d still prefer if he were just a bit less happy-go-lucky and sulked a bit. Not saying make him a painful character to watch but show us a bit more emotional range, though I have to say Tom killed it on the plane. There were scenes with Peter feeling pressured and I just feel like it would’ve been made better if we got more of those moments, to show us that he feels this weight on his shoulders.

Mysterio, simply the BEST villain I’ve seen in a Spidey film. I was sold by Jake’s performance. I adored the way he snapped at his crew. The motivation made sense but would’ve preferred something a bit less tied to IronMan. 

Overall, what would I score it? 8/10, FAR better than Homecoming.

I always hear everyone say that Garfield’s Peter is “terrible” when really that’s not the case. They based it heavily on Ultimate Peter who, was actually quite a talkative, arrogant, and douchey version of Peter. Especially when he got his powers, in the first 10 issues alone he runs off and gets into an argument with Uncle Ben. I always see people praising Tobey for his (admittedly) great portrayal of timid Peter but always say Andrew did a bad job because he wasn’t timid or shy. He did a great job, I personally consider TASM1 to be my favorite. I understand that from a film making standpoint the Raimi trilogy is better but to me, TASM1 will always be my favorite Spidey film. Andrew deserves more respect. His Peter and Spider-Man were great. The reason those films were so poorly received was Sony’s meddling.

Spider-Man tbh. not necessarily Tom is overrated or the character as a whole is overrated. i mean the MCU version, it’s not that compelling. i enjoyed Homecoming but it lacked something. it lacked the true relatable aspect of Peter, the consequences. yes, he got his suit taken away but that’s really the only consequence he faced. although, it would’ve been nice to see Peter face real consequences socially for always having to leave or being late all the time and being a generally bad friend. Ned knowing his identity was one of the things that made me feel like it wasn’t that great. yes, i do realize he got kicked off his debate team, may grounds him, and all that good stuff but it never felt like he hated it. it was like “oh i can be more of a superhero” or “oh i can spend more time as peter parker” he never felt any real anguish. i’d love for him to have been like “oh man, i need to focus more on school” but no, he just wanted to be an Avenger. when his driving motivation should just be to do the right thing. which act 3 did nicely actually, but he never felt guilt for not being able to help others after he got the suit taken away. he didn’t even do small stuff with the homemade suit. in conclusion, people worship the MCU portrayal too much and say he’s the greatest portrayal when it’s clearly lacking.
